object: The Fifth Solvay International Conference on Physics, held 24–29 October 1927 in Brussels. Twenty-nine physicists — seventeen of them Nobel laureates — gathered to debate "Electrons and Photons." The Bohr-Einstein debates that erupted here defined the philosophical fault lines of twentieth-century physics and marked the moment determinism lost its hold on science.
